clue.text: Blows into hose

blocks.note: first meaning: punches, as a verb in 'he ... him'... here the plural noun, hard hits
second meaning: stockings or short stockings worn on the feet

explanation.surface: Someone blows air into a garden hose to clear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a garden pipe, but it is the old word for legwear; 'Blows' are hard punches.
explanation.definitionFit: A sock is a hard punch, and hose is the traditional collective word for stockings and footwear.

clue.text: Jewish caper dish (not orthodox)

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from convention, so the letters abandon their usual order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kosher-style dish made with capers that breaks with strict tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not orthodox' sounds like a comment on religious practice; it is telling you to put the letters in an unconventional order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sephardic Jews descend from the communities of Spain and Portugal, so the adjective describes one branch of Jewish people.

clue.text: Cold ventilator is stuck fast

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lung ventilates the body, drawing air in and out

explanation.surface: A cold air vent has jammed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ventilator' suggests a machine or air duct; here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, to grip tightly or adhere firmly to something.

clue.text: It may be used to conceal one's position in the field

definitions.text: It may be used to conceal one's position in the field

blocks.clueFragment: It may be used to conceal one's position in the field
blocks.note: surface reading: something a cricketer or farmer uses to hide where they stand in a meadow
setter's reading: the battlefield, where soldiers throw a device releasing a screen of cover

explanation.surface: Some trick a player uses to hide where they are standing on a sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The field' suggests sport or farming; it is the field of battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers throw a canister releasing a dense cloud to hide their movements from the enemy.

clue.text: Good books that don't always achieve recognition

definitions.text: Good books that don't always achieve recognition

blocks.clueFragment: Good books that don't always achieve recognition
blocks.note: surface reading: worthy novels that never get the fame they deserve
setter's reading: books of the Bible (the Good Book) that churches do not all accept as canonical

explanation.surface: Fine literature that is often overlooked by critics and prize juries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good books' points to the Good Book, the Bible; 'recognition' is acceptance into the canon, not literary fame.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are scriptural writings that some churches include in the Bible and others reject as uncanonical.

clue.text: Place the landed gentry soon leave

definitions.text: Place the landed gentry soon leave

blocks.clueFragment: Place the landed gentry soon leave
blocks.note: surface reading: a country estate that aristocratic landowners will shortly quit
setter's reading: people whose plane has just touched down, who soon head out of the terminal

explanation.surface: An estate that the landowning aristocracy will soon abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed gentry' are landowning families; here 'landed' means just off a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers who have just come down from a flight soon depart from the terminal where aircraft arrive.

clue.text: Old-fashioned clothes last longer

blocks.note: out of date, as in 'flares are out'
wear means clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: Dated garments are more durable.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to remain in use for more time than it does, outlasting it.

clue.text: Miserable fellow loses wicket to heave

indicators.note: the miserable fellow gives up something, so the cricket abbreviation drops out of his word

blocks.note: a wretch is an unhappy or contemptible person
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: An unhappy batsman loses his wicket and throws up in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to make the motion of vomiting, a gagging spasm of the stomach and throat.

clue.text: Drink and smoke inside — it makes a smell!

indicators.note: smoke goes inside the drink, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: perry is an alcoholic drink made from pears
fume is smoke or vapour

explanation.surface: Drinking and smoking indoors leaves a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry is pear cider, a drink more familiar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfumery is a place where scents are manufactured, so it produces fragrances.

clue.text: In agreement to make amends

blocks.note: in agreement or harmony

explanation.surface: Two parties settle their differences by making up.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself comes from 'at one', reconciled.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone for a wrong is to make reparation or redress for it.

clue.text: Nabob's dog and cat run inside

indicators.note: the run happens inside the cat, so that letter is placed within the animal's word

blocks.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's cartoon dog
taken as written; it holds the next piece
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rich man owns a dog and a cat that dash about indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nabob's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'has' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very wealthy, powerful person, originally a returning East India Company fortune-maker; a plutocrat rules through wealth.

clue.text: Trunk noisily pulled apart thus

indicators.note: noisily means out loud, so the words are taken by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: pulled apart is tore, and thus is so; said together they make the answer

explanation.surface: A tree trunk was loudly ripped in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a tree or luggage; here it is the human body without head and limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is the part between neck and hips, which anatomists and sculptors call by this Italian word.

clue.text: Point of view that may be obtuse

blocks.note: first meaning: a standpoint or approach to a subject
second meaning: a figure in geometry measured in degrees, one over ninety being obtuse

explanation.surface: A stubborn, dim-witted opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtuse' seems to call the opinion stupid; in geometry it describes a wide corner between two lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist's slant on a story is its particular perspective, and in geometry such a corner wider than a right one is obtuse.

clue.text: Something for everyone where this is kept

definitions.text: Something for everyone where this is kept

blocks.clueFragment: Something for everyone where this is kept
blocks.note: surface reading: a store or shop that stocks items to suit every customer
setter's reading: the idiom of keeping a home where all visitors are welcome at any time

explanation.surface: A shop that stocks something to please every customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept' reads like stock on a shelf; the idiom is 'to keep' this, offering hospitality to all comers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps this offers hospitality to any guest who calls; it is also an event where visitors may tour a home.

clue.text: Get Jack out of the cooler

definitions.text: Get Jack out of the cooler

blocks.clueFragment: Get Jack out of the cooler
blocks.note: surface reading: spring a man named Jack from prison, the cooler being slang for jail
setter's reading: Jack Frost, the personification of frost, removed from a fridge or freezer

explanation.surface: A plan to break a prisoner called Jack out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cooler' is slang for prison, but here it is a fridge; Jack is Jack Frost, the figure of icy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw a freezer or frozen food is to remove its ice, a verb built from a prefix meaning removal and the icy coating.

clue.text: Apartment borrowed from you sounds windy

indicators.note: sounds asks for how the pronoun is pronounced, giving a single letter that is said the same way

blocks.note: a flat is a British apartment
the letter U is said like the word you
if something is borrowed from you, you lent it

explanation.surface: A flat someone borrowed from you is noisy with draughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' looks like part of 'sounds windy'; it only tells you to take the word you by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent means suffering from intestinal gas, so a windy person in the bodily sense.

clue.text: Girls' school novel — read one

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or original, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's reading assignment: pick one novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun for a book to read; it is an adjective meaning new, so the letters take a new order. ROEDEAN is a famous girls' boarding school near Brighton in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known independent boarding school for girls on the Sussex coast of England.

clue.text: Play bill

blocks.note: first meaning: a performance or acting out of a scene
second meaning: a law passed by parliament, which began as a draft statute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play bill' reads as a theatre programme, a playbill; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the acting out of something on stage and a statute or law that has been passed.

clue.text: You can write on this for a fiver weekly, perhaps

blocks.note: a fiver is a five-pound note, British slang
a weekly is a newspaper published every week

explanation.surface: Writing paper sold for five pounds a week.
explanation.walkthrough: A fiver is a British five-pound banknote; 'perhaps' shows a weekly is just one kind of newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery sheets for letters are what you write on, so the definition describes the answer by its use.

clue.text: It's hot in the banking hall

indicators.note: the hot is said to be in the banking, so its letter goes within that word

blocks.note: a camber is the banking or slope of a road surface
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A bank's main hall is uncomfortably warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' suggests finance, but it is the tilt of a road, a camber.
explanation.definitionFit: A large formal room such as a council chamber or the chamber of a parliament is a hall for assemblies.

clue.text: A platform for the beak

blocks.note: first meaning: a raised stand for a speaker or conductor
second meaning: a zoological term for a bird's bill or snout

explanation.surface: A raised stand for the magistrate in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which makes the surface a judge's dais; here it is a bird's bill, the zoological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a speaker's raised stage, and in zoology the hard projecting bill of a bird or insect.

clue.text: They say the girl has a heel for a shrink

indicators.note: they say points to what people speak aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a girl's name, Anna, plus list, which is to heel over like a ship

explanation.surface: Gossip that a young woman with a shoe heel needs a therapist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like part of a shoe; it is the verb for a ship leaning, which is to list.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is informal slang for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst, short for headshrinker.

clue.text: Forming a ring to do away with a king

blocks.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish
taken as written
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries form a circle to plot getting rid of their monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means shaped like a circle with a hole in the middle, as in an annular eclipse.

clue.text: Counts are a push-over for such a woman

indicators.note: pushing the letters over knocks them out of place, so they fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Noblemen with titles are an easy conquest for a seductive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counts' looks like noblemen and 'push-over' like an easy target; the push knocks the letters over into a new order. The definition leans on the surface, which suggests her trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a woman is one who would find counts easy prey: a high-class mistress kept by rich or noble lovers.

clue.text: Maker of varnish is a firm friend

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A varnish manufacturer is a reliable, loyal friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maker of varnish' sounds like a company, but it is the raw material, a tree resin used for varnishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard tropical tree resin used as an ingredient in making lacquers and varnishes.

clue.text: Garment cut in pieces

indicators.note: in pieces means broken up, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing is cut up by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like tailoring, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose, often belted, item of clothing reaching to the hips or knees.

clue.text: Sort of wood that has a bloom

blocks.note: first meaning: the timber of the American ... tree, used in cabinet making
second meaning: a spring bulb flower

explanation.surface: A kind of tree that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulipwood is a pale timber from the tulip tree, and the same word names the cup-shaped spring flower grown from a bulb.

clue.text: Melon could be a failure

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else when rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A melon might turn out to be a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a fruit, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a lemon is a dud or flop, especially a defective car or product.

clue.text: Swan circling about to tidy its feathers

indicators.note: the swan circles something, going round it, so its word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A swan swims round in a circle while grooming itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The female swan is a pen and the male a cob, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom their plumage with their beaks, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Chart showing where golfers get a free drop?

definitions.text: Chart showing where golfers get a free drop

blocks.clueFragment: Chart showing where golfers get a free drop?
blocks.note: surface reading: a course plan marking spots where a golfer may drop the ball without penalty
setter's reading: in golf, taking a free drop is called taking this; the chart also shows hills and valleys

explanation.surface: A golf course map marking the places a player may drop a ball without penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, permission to lift and drop the ball without penalty is called taking relief; the chart is actually one showing hills and valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a chart shows the height of land by shading or modelling, depicting the terrain's raised and lowered surfaces.

clue.text: Recent arrival who can always find a waiter

definitions.text: Recent arrival who can always find a waiter

blocks.clueFragment: who can always find a waiter
blocks.note: surface reading: a diner who never has trouble getting service in a restaurant
setter's reading: someone who turns up after time always finds a person kept waiting

explanation.surface: A newcomer to town who is always well served in restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiter' suggests restaurant staff, but it means anyone left waiting by someone unpunctual.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who arrives after the appointed time has just turned up, and others will have been kept waiting.

clue.text: Singer's settled course of progress

blocks.note: first meaning: a high male voice
second meaning: the general drift or steady course

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a high adult male voice and also the steady, even course of something, as in 'the even tenor of his ways'.
